commits.title: One part sheet for all of a page's rows, with the theme layers read once per article

changes.how: Optional second part: do it only after commit 1 is deployed and green. Keep it only if every check below passes, including the e2e count case and modals.spec.ts, visibility.spec.ts and responsive-parity.spec.ts; if any fails, revert this commit (see stop_if). (1) Add an async server component `ArticleStyles({ rows, place }: { rows: PageRow[]; place: GridPlace })`: `const layers = place.theme ?? (await themeLayersFor(place.owner));` then, for a place with an owner, `const base = await storeLinkBase(place.owner, place.market)` and map rows through `withStoreLinks(row, base)` when base is set (exactly what `StoreRowView` does per row today); then `const themed = themedRows(rows, layers.elements, layers.sections);` and return `<PartStyles rows={themed} owner={place.owner} />`. (2) In `PageArticle`, draw `<ArticleStyles rows={rows} place={place} />` once, directly after the `<CustomCss ...>` line and before `rows.map`, and pass a new prop `styled` (true) to each `PageRowView`. (3) Add `styled?: boolean` to PageRowView's props and pass it through StoreRowView, ThemedRowView and RowView; in `RowView` draw `<PartStyles rows={[row]} owner={place.owner} />` only when `styled` is not true. Everything else in RowView stays. The class names are hashes of each element's rules (`kzr-`), so one sheet for all rows holds the same rules as the per-row sheets; a modal's row and a row behind a visibility hole get theirs from the article's sheet, which is outside the holes.

In `SiteRows` (about line 335) do the same for a header's or footer's rows: draw `<ArticleStyles rows={rows} place={place} />` (export it from page-article.tsx) once before `rows.map`, and pass `styled` to each `PageRowView`.
